key_insight: A validated FEM model can generate high-quality synthetic tactile deformation data that trains a fast GNN surrogate for real-time, sub-millimeter prediction.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables accurate soft tactile sensor simulation and design exploration without costly repeated physical testing or minute-scale FEM runs.
method: Use 82 real camera-tracked contact cases to tune and validate the ANSYS FEM model.
Generate 768 synthetic contact scenarios from the validated FEM for GNN training.
Train a graph neural network for both forward and inverse tactile deformation prediction, then deploy it in a real-time visualization pipeline.
evidence_signal: The validated FEM achieved under 0.5 mm error in over 90% of validation cases, and the GNN reached 0.32 mm mean absolute error with millisecond inference.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a planar 2D tactile structure, so broader performance on more complex 3D soft sensors may require additional validation.
paper_title: FEM-Validated Real-Time Modelling of Soft Tactile Deformation
